headline: High risk of data leakage and capability conflict: Nullclaw’s broad file/network/tool access can collide with Airflow’s automation and egress, while prompt-injection risk is limited by lack of a direct shared channel.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Airflow has no browser or filesystem write surface, while Nullclaw can read/write files, use MCP, and run browsers. A direct injection bridge is not documented, so the main pathway is unusual manual or file-based handoff rather than default parsing. Uncertainty keeps this above none.
conditions: IF Airflow outputs are manually copied into Nullclaw prompts or files
IF Nullclaw is configured to ingest workspace files as instructions
mitigations: Keep Airflow and Nullclaw in separate directories
Disable any file-to-prompt ingestion in Nullclaw
Use read-only exports from Airflow
Add a human review step before copying outputs
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for imported content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Nullclaw touches API keys, private keys, bearer tokens, workspace files, and audit logs, and it has broad filesystem and network egress. Airflow is a data-engineering orchestrator with broad egress. A shared workspace or copied artifacts could expose sensitive material through Nullclaw’s outputs or network calls.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace or exported files
IF Nullclaw is given files containing secrets or tokens
mitigations: Store secrets outside any shared workspace
Restrict Nullclaw to a scrubbed dataset
Rotate any tokens used in shared files
Review outbound destinations for Nullclaw
requires-engineering: enforce secret redaction before handoff

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Nullclaw can write the filesystem, modify git state, spawn subprocesses, and use MCP; Airflow can also drive automation and broad egress. If both operate on the same repo or workspace, concurrent writes and git mutations can corrupt state or overwrite each other. The pairwise conflict is plausible in default operator setups.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or git repository
IF Airflow tasks and Nullclaw sessions run concurrently
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Pause one agent during the other’s write phase
Use git locks or serialized commits
Limit Nullclaw to read-only mode for shared repos
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Nullclaw can act on files, webhooks, and shell commands, so if it consumes Airflow-generated outputs as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions. Airflow’s automation role increases the chance that its outputs are treated as operational truth. No verification bridge is documented, so this is inferred rather than directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Airflow output is fed into Nullclaw without validation
IF Nullclaw is allowed to execute actions based on Airflow-produced artifacts
mitigations: Require schema validation on Airflow outputs
Add a manual approval step before execution
Log and diff all downstream actions
Limit Nullclaw to read-only review mode
requires-engineering: implement provenance checks between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Nullclaw explicitly handles secrets, audit logs, and workspace files, while Airflow is a data-engineering orchestrator with broad egress. If regulated data or secrets are routed through both, retention and residency controls may diverge. No specific residency or certification mismatch is documented, so this remains a moderate compliance risk.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in Nullclaw workspace files or logs
IF Airflow sends those artifacts to external services
mitigations: Classify data before routing it to either agent
Disable logging of sensitive fields
Keep regulated data out of shared workspaces
Review retention settings for both systems
requires-engineering: align residency and retention policies
